provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The grand old Duke of York
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the words of the rhyme
The pupils should be able to perform up and down actions

Introduction:
Last term we learned action rhymes. Today we learn a marching rhyme.

Content:
The grand old Duke of York had ten thousand men
He marched them up to the top of the hill
He marched them down again

Class activity:
Stand up and march on the spot
When we sing up march high
When we sing down bend low

Evaluation questions:
What does the Duke do with his men?
Show me the up action
Show me the down action

Summary:
We enjoyed marching up and down to this rhyme.

topics.title: Here we go round the mulberry bush
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the main verse
The pupils should be able to add daily task verses

Introduction:
Last week we marched. This week we do daily tasks in a song.

Content:
Here we go round the mulberry bush
The mulberry bush
The mulberry bush
Here we go round the mulberry bush
So early in the morning

Class activity:
Hold hands and go in a circle
Add verses like this is the way we wash our hands

Evaluation questions:
What plant do we go round?
What do we do in the morning?
Can you make up a new verse?

Summary:
We sang about daily tasks in this fun circle song.

topics.title: Sing a song of sixpence
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count twenty blackbirds
The pupils should be able to act as king and queen

Introduction:
Today we learn a rhyme about birds and royalty.

Content:
Sing a song of sixpence
A pocket full of rye
Four and twenty blackbirds
Baked in a pie

Class activity:
Count to twenty on fingers
Take turns being the king who eats the pie

Evaluation questions:
How many blackbirds are in the pie?
What is in the pocket?
Show me how a king eats pie

Summary:
We enjoyed counting and pretending to be royalty.

topics.title: Little Jack Horner
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme
The pupils should be able to discuss good behaviour

Introduction:
Last week we were kings and queens. This week we learn about Jack.

Content:
Little Jack Horner sat in a corner
Eating a Christmas pie
He put in his thumb
And pulled out a plum
And said what a good boy am I

Class activity:
Sit in a circle like Jack
Pull out a pretend plum and show it

Evaluation questions:
What is Jack eating?
What does Jack pull out?
Is it good to show off?

Summary:
We learned about not showing off like Jack.

topics.title: Georgie Porgie
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme
The pupils should be able to explain kind behaviour

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jack. Today we learn about Georgie.

Content:
Georgie Porgie pudding and pie
Kissed the girls and made them cry
When the boys came out to play
Georgie Porgie ran away

Class activity:
Walk around then run away when boys come
Practice asking to play nicely

Evaluation questions:
What does Georgie do to the girls?
What happens when boys come?
How should we ask to play?

Summary:
We learned to be kind friends like good children.

topics.title: Doctor Foster
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme
The pupils should be able to talk about different weather

Introduction:
Last week we learned about friends. Today we learn about weather.

Content:
Doctor Foster went to Gloucester
In a shower of rain
He stepped in a puddle
Right up to his middle
And never went there again

Class activity:
Stomp feet for rain steps
Jump over pretend puddles

Evaluation questions:
Where did Doctor Foster go?
What weather did he meet?
What happened to his feet?

Summary:
We learned about rain and puddles in this rhyme.

topics.title: There was an old woman
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the shoe rhyme
The pupils should be able to count to ten

Introduction:
Today we learn a rhyme about an old woman and many children.

Content:
There was an old woman who lived in a shoe
She had so many children she didn't know what to do

Class activity:
Count ten children in the class
Pretend to rock a baby in a shoe

Evaluation questions:
Where did the old woman live?
How many children did she have?
Can you count to ten?

Summary:
We enjoyed counting and talking about the shoe house.

topics.title: Sea shell rhyme
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the shell rhyme
The pupils should be able to listen to sea sounds

Introduction:
Last week we counted children. This week we listen to the sea.

Content:
Sea shell sea shell
By the deep blue sea
Hold it to your ear
And what do you see

Class activity:
Pass around real shells
Hold shells to ears to hear the sea

Evaluation questions:
What do we do with shells?
What do we hear in shells?
Can you make a wave sound?

Summary:
We loved listening to the sea in the shells.

topics.title: Our class rhyme
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a short rhyme
The pupils should be able to perform with actions

Introduction:
Today we make our own special class rhyme.

Content:
Think of things we do in class
Make short lines about them

Class activity:
Sit in a circle and add one line each
Add actions to each line

Evaluation questions:
What is our rhyme about?
Can you do the action for your line?
What rhymes with our topic?

Summary:
We created and performed our own class rhyme.

topics.title: Graduation rhyme concert
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform favourite rhymes
The pupils should be able to sing alone

Introduction:
Today we show all we learned this term in a concert.

Content:
Sing all the rhymes we learned
Take turns to sing alone

Class activity:
Line up and perform each rhyme
Clap for each friend who performs

Evaluation questions:
Which rhyme is your favourite?
Can you sing a rhyme alone?
 Who performed best today?

Summary:
We had fun showing our rhymes at our concert.
